definition: A contraction of καί and ἐγώ: and I, or I also, even I.
First person singular possessive adjective: belonging to me, mine.
Adverb: no more, no longer, not any further.
Second person singular reflexive pronoun: yourself, pointing back to the one addressed.
First person singular reflexive pronoun: myself, pointing back to the speaker.
Second person singular possessive adjective: belonging to you, yours.
Conjunction introducing an outcome to be avoided: lest, so that not.
Introduces a tentative question or possibility: perhaps, whether perhaps.
Adverb: not ever, at no time.
A contraction of καί and ἐκεῖνος: and that one, and he, or that one also.
An exclamation rejecting something as unthinkable: far be it, God forbid.
A contraction of καί and ἐάν: and if, or even if, introducing a condition.
Even just, at least, as in touching only the edge of a garment.
Second person plural possessive adjective: belonging to you all, yours.
A contraction of καί and ἐκεῖθεν: and from there, or and after that.
A contraction of καί and ἐκεῖ: and there, or there also.
Verb stem that supplies passive forms of 'say', as in 'it was said'.
Part of the name Valley of the Son of Hinnom, a ravine on the south side of Jerusalem, later a site of child sacrifice.
First person plural possessive adjective: belonging to us, ours.
Aramaic third person feminine pronoun: she, it, also used to mean 'is'.
Conjunction: if indeed, if after all, since. A strengthened 'if'.
Interrogative adverb from ἵνα τί: for what purpose, why?
Strengthened negative particle in the phrase 'but if not', meaning otherwise.
A tenth part, especially a tenth of goods given as a tithe.
Adjective: gentle, meek, mild, not harsh or self-assertive.
A female slave or bondservant, a handmaid.
The suffix 'their' on 'their king' (malkam), which is also read as Milcom, the god of the Ammonites.
The Valley of Elah ('terebinth') in the lowland of Judah, where David fought Goliath.
An imperative of ἄγω used as an interjection: come now, look here.
Adverb: exceedingly, beyond measure, used of the so-called super-apostles.
Adverb: not yet.
An attack or a stirring up, as of a crowd into a riot.
A pressing burden that bears down on someone day after day.
Conjunction: and yet, although, nevertheless.
Part of the name of the Old Gate (Jeshanah Gate) of Jerusalem, repaired under Nehemiah.
A spelling of Damascus, the chief city of Aram (Syria).
A Benjaminite archer who joined David at Ziklag.
A Gadite, the eighth of the leaders who joined David in the wilderness.
A town of Judah, also called Kiriath-jearim, from which David brought up the ark.
A town on the border of Ephraim, east of Shechem.
'Wells of the sons of Jaakan', a stopping place of Israel in the wilderness.

'High places of Baal', a town on the heights of Moab near the Arnon, later given to Reuben.
'Bramble', the name of the threshing floor beyond the Jordan where Jacob was mourned.
To be or become filthy, in a moral sense to be defiled.
A drug or potion, in a bad sense a magic potion or sorcery.
To shine through, of the day, to dawn.
Suffering of hardship or misfortune, and patient endurance in it.
To keep back or fail to pay what is due, as wages held back.
A doing or performing, the act of carrying something out.
A festive assembly of a whole people gathered to celebrate.
Particle: surely, of course, as everyone knows.
Freedom from corruption, soundness and integrity, especially in teaching.
To bring someone to their senses, to train or urge them to self-control.
To put someone under oath, to charge solemnly.
To feel affection for someone and yearn after them.
The new moon, the first day of the month, kept as a festival.
Adverb: with pure motives, sincerely.
To arrange or get something ready in advance.
Aramaic verb in the phrase 'maranatha': come! (Our Lord, come!).
Aramaic 'our Lord' in the phrase 'maranatha', a prayer for the Lord to come.
Particle in an argument from lesser to greater: let alone, how much more.
Adjective: persuasive, convincing.
To fasten onto or lay hold of, as the viper on Paul's hand.
To join others in assailing someone, here by adding charges.
A setting right, an improvement or reform made in a nation.
Feminine of νέος 'new', in the city name Neapolis, the port of Philippi.
To lean toward someone and attach oneself to them, as followers to a leader.
A cooling or refreshing, relief and renewal.
Adjective: sinless, not having sinned.
Caught in the very act of a crime.
A pool in Jerusalem by the Sheep Gate, with five porches, where Jesus healed a lame man.
Conjunction: and yet, although indeed.
A small coin, in the plural small change.
Comparative adverb: farther, further on.
To disturb or upset, in the passive to be distracted or troubled.
Conjunction: when, at the time that.
Adjective: deadly, fatal, used of a deadly drink or poison.
The day before the Sabbath, the day of preparation.
To be weighed down or heavy, as eyes heavy with sleep.
Adverb: exceedingly, beyond all measure.
On (Heliopolis) in Egypt, spelled as 'Aven', a pun on the word for wickedness.

A cry of lament: woe.
A captain of the forces, son of the Maacathite, who came to Gedaliah at Mizpah.
Of a storm, to whirl or rage on without stopping.
Aramaic demonstrative pronoun: these.
Father of the man whom Aram and Israel planned to set up as king of Judah in place of Ahaz.

'Valley of craftsmen', a place near Lod settled by craftsmen of Judah.

A Levite who sealed the covenant under Nehemiah.
Father of Zadok, who repaired part of the wall of Jerusalem.
A son of Bani who had married a foreign wife after the exile.

A son of Zattu who had married a foreign wife after the exile.
'The small one', father of Johanan, who returned from exile with Ezra.
Aramaic form of Moses, the lawgiver of Israel, cited for the book of Moses.
Father of Shaphat, David's overseer of the herds in the valleys.

A person from Shepham or Siphmoth, used of Zabdi, David's overseer of the wine stores.

Head of the eighteenth division of priests under David.
A Gershonite Levite, son of Shimei, also called Zizah.
A person from Mezobah, used of Jaasiel, one of David's mighty men.

Father of Naarai, one of David's mighty men.
Father of Eliphal, one of David's mighty men.
A man of Manasseh, son of Shemida.

'Valley of craftsmen', a place near Lod settled by craftsmen of Judah.

Part of Ir-nahash, 'city of the serpent', a town or founder in the genealogy of Judah.
A son of Ashhur in the genealogy of Judah, or the clan of the Ahashtarites.
A descendant of David after the exile, son of Elioenai.

A person from Eshtaol, a town in the lowland of Judah.

Father of one of Solomon's district officers (Ben-deker).
A person from Arab in Judah, used of Paarai, one of David's mighty men.
A person from Bahurim, used of Azmaveth, one of David's mighty men.
A name given to the chief of David's mighty men, in a difficult text.

Part of the name Beth-maacah, a town in the far north closely tied to Abel (Abel-beth-maacah).
Part of the name Beth-maacah, a town in the far north closely tied to Abel (Abel-beth-maacah).
A forest in Judah where David hid from Saul.
'Valley of hyenas', a valley in Benjamin facing the wilderness.
To feed animals with mixed fodder.
The town in Gilead where the judge Jair was buried.
A place in the Jordan valley toward which the Midianites fled from Gideon.
Part of Me-jarkon, 'waters of Jarkon', a place or stream in the land of Dan.
A town on the border of Issachar.
A town of Benjamin, probably Kiriath-jearim.
Part of Zelah-eleph (Haeleph), a town of Benjamin.
Part of Chephar-ammoni, 'village of the Ammonites', a town of Benjamin.
'Wells of the sons of Jaakan', a stopping place of Israel in the wilderness.
'Watchers', the field of Zophim on top of Pisgah where Balak took Balaam.
